intent.raw_query: Maldives honeymoon for 2, $5000 budget, snorkeling and luxury resorts, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: North Malé Atoll, near Veligandu or Baros Island Boutique Stay
selected_hotel.location: North Malé Atoll, near Veligandu or Baros Island

experiences.name: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne
experiences.description: Embark on a traditional Maldivian wooden dhoni boat chartered exclusively for two, sailing through turquoise lagoons as the sun dips below the horizon. Enjoy chilled champagne, fresh tropical fruit platters, and a private butler while dolphins often accompany the vessel. A quintessential romantic experience perfectly suited for honeymooners seeking intimacy and natural beauty.
experiences.location: North Malé Atoll, near Veligandu or Baros Island

experiences.name: Coral Reef Snorkeling Safari at Hanifaru Bay
experiences.description: Join a guided snorkeling safari to Hanifaru Bay, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve renowned for its spectacular congregation of manta rays and whale sharks. Glide through crystal-clear waters teeming with vibrant coral gardens, sea turtles, and exotic reef fish. A small-group guided tour ensures an intimate, eco-conscious experience that is both thrilling and unforgettable for snorkeling enthusiasts.

experiences.name: Underwater Spa Treatment
experiences.description: Indulge in a signature couples massage at an overwater or semi-submerged spa pavilion with a glass floor, allowing you to watch colorful marine life drift beneath you as skilled therapists perform traditional Maldivian healing rituals using coconut oil and local botanicals. This ultra-luxurious experience blends wellness, romance, and the mesmerizing underwater world into one serene session.
experiences.location: Rangali Island, South Ari Atoll (Conrad Maldives area)

experiences.name: Private Sandbank Picnic Dining Experience
experiences.description: Be whisked away by speedboat to a secluded, uninhabited white sandbank in the middle of the Indian Ocean, where a personal chef and butler set up a gourmet candlelit picnic just for two. Savor freshly grilled Maldivian lobster, sashimi-grade tuna, tropical salads, and artisan desserts while surrounded by nothing but endless blue ocean and sky — the ultimate honeymoon memory.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cultural Village Tour & Traditional Cooking Class
experiences.description: Visit the inhabited local island of Maafushi or Hulhumalé to explore authentic Maldivian culture, including a guided walk through a traditional fishing village, a visit to a historic mosque, and a hands-on cooking class where a local family teaches you to prepare classic dishes like mas huni (tuna and coconut), garudhiya fish broth, and sweet bondibai rice pudding. A meaningful cultural immersion that complements the luxury resort experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Maldives
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: North Malé Atoll, near Veligandu or Baros Island Boutique Stay
hotel.location: North Malé Atoll, near Veligandu or Baros Island

experiences.name: Maldivian Cultural Village Tour & Traditional Cooking Class
experiences.description: Visit the inhabited local island of Maafushi or Hulhumalé to explore authentic Maldivian culture, including a guided walk through a traditional fishing village, a visit to a historic mosque, and a hands-on cooking class where a local family teaches you to prepare classic dishes like mas huni (tuna and coconut), garudhiya fish broth, and sweet bondibai rice pudding. A meaningful cultural immersion that complements the luxury resort experience.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and collect luggage. Take a budget-friendly public ferry or shared speedboat transfer to North Malé Atoll accommodation near Veligandu or Baros Island. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the beach to get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Watch your first Maldivian sunset from the beach or your guesthouse deck. Enjoy a relaxed welcome evening exploring the local area around your boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick snack at Velana Airport (budget MVR 50–80)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a local café near the ferry terminal – try short eats like bajiya or hedhikaa (MVR 30–60)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local island restaurant near your guesthouse – try mas riha (tuna curry) with roshi bread (MVR 80–150 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry or shared speedboat transfer in advance to save money. Public ferries cost as little as MVR 10–20 vs. private speedboats at $80+. Keep some MVR cash handy for small purchases on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling session directly from the house reef near your guesthouse. Most boutique stays in North Malé Atoll offer free or low-cost reef access. Look for vibrant coral gardens, reef sharks, and tropical fish. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible to avoid rental costs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget group snorkeling day trip organized by your guesthouse or a local tour operator. Visit 2–3 nearby snorkel spots including a coral garden and a sandbank. Many operators offer trips for $25–40 per person including equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic beachside stroll at sunset. Collect shells and enjoy the calm lagoon waters. Return to guesthouse for a cozy evening.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast if included, or visit a local café for black tea, roshi, and mas huni (shredded tuna with coconut – a Maldivian staple) (MVR 40–70)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a local shop for the snorkel trip – buy fresh fruit, crackers, and juice (MVR 50–80)
meals.dinner: Local island restaurant dinner – try garudhiya (tuna broth soup) with rice and pickle (MVR 100–160)

day_by_day.notes: The house reef snorkeling is often the best value activity in the Maldives. Ask your guesthouse host for the best entry points and tide timings. Sunrise snorkeling offers the calmest water and best visibility.

day_by_day.morning: Maldivian Cultural Village Tour & Traditional Cooking Class – Take the organized experience to visit the inhabited local island of Maafushi or Hulhumalé. Explore the narrow streets, visit a local mosque, and learn about traditional Maldivian crafts and lifestyle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in the hands-on traditional cooking class component of the cultural tour. Learn to prepare authentic Maldivian dishes such as mas huni, bis keemiya (stuffed pastries), and fresh coconut sambal. Enjoy your prepared meal together as a group.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your guesthouse by late afternoon. Enjoy a peaceful evening on the beach, stargazing from the shore – the Maldives offers spectacular night skies away from city light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Local café breakfast – roshi with egg and tea (MVR 50–80)
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Cultural Village Tour & Cooking Class experience
meals.dinner: Cook something simple at guesthouse if kitchen available, or budget local eatery – fish curry and rice (MVR 80–130)

day_by_day.notes: The Cultural Village Tour is one of the best budget-friendly experiences in the Maldives, offering authentic insight into local life. Dress modestly when visiting local islands – cover shoulders and knees out of respect for Islamic customs.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) session in the calm lagoon near your guesthouse. Many budget guesthouses offer free or cheap kayak rentals. Paddle around the sandbank and enjoy the serene morning atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby sandbank (sandbank hopping is a quintessential Maldives experience). Your guesthouse can arrange a shared boat trip to a deserted sandbank for $15–25 per person. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and taking romantic photos on the pristine white sand.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a DIY romantic beach picnic – buy fresh fruit, local snacks, and a non-alcoholic drink from a local shop. Watch the sunset together from the sandbank or beach.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café – fresh tropical fruit plate with yogurt and tea (MVR 60–90)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and light bites for the sandbank trip – local bakery items, fresh coconut (MVR 60–100)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a nicer local restaurant dinner for a romantic evening – grilled fresh tuna or lobster if budget allows (MVR 200–350 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sandbank trips are weather-dependent. Confirm with your guesthouse the evening before. Bring sunscreen, hats, and plenty of water as there is no shade on sandbanks. This is a perfect honeymoon/romance photo opportunity.

day_by_day.morning: Dolphin watching cruise – book a shared group sunrise or morning dolphin cruise through your guesthouse or local operator ($20–35 per person). Spinner dolphins are commonly spotted in North Malé Atoll waters. A truly magical experience for couples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from cruise and rest during the hottest part of the day. Enjoy the guesthouse pool or lagoon. Read, relax, and recharge in true island style.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local island's Friday market (Jumma market) if available. Browse local produce, fresh fish, and handmade crafts. Friday is a special day in the Maldives as it is the holy day – observe local customs respectfully.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before dolphin cruise – dates, tea, and a pastry (MVR 30–50)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant lunch after returning from cruise – tuna sandwich or short eats (MVR 60–100)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish dinner at a beachside local eatery – ask for the daily catch (MVR 120–180)

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin sightings are not guaranteed but are very common in this region. The best viewing is typically at sunrise or just before sunset. Bring a light jacket for the early morning boat ride as it can be breezy on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day snorkeling excursion to a famous snorkel site in North Malé Atoll – consider Banana Reef or HP Reef (Blue Lagoon), two of the Maldives' most celebrated snorkel/dive spots accessible by day trip. Book a shared group trip ($30–50 per person including equipment and guide).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snorkel excursion visiting a second reef site. Look for sea turtles, eagle rays, and diverse coral formations. Many day trips include a stop at a local island for lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to guesthouse by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a couple's massage if your guesthouse offers budget spa services, or simply unwind on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast – eggs, toast, fruit, and coffee (MVR 70–100)
meals.lunch: Included in day trip or local island lunch stop – rice and curry (MVR 80–120)
meals.dinner: Romantic candlelit dinner at your guesthouse restaurant or a nearby local spot – request a beachside table (MVR 180–280 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: Banana Reef is one of the Maldives' most iconic snorkel sites with exceptional marine biodiversity. Book the day trip the evening before to secure spots. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning – sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. This is your mid-trip rest day. Spend the morning reading on the beach, journaling, or simply floating in the lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local island's community areas and interact with friendly locals. Visit a local school or community center if permitted. Browse a local handicraft shop for souvenirs – lacquerware, woven mats, and coral jewelry are traditional Maldivian crafts (support local artisans).
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent beach walk – if conditions are right (new moon period), the beaches of North Malé Atoll can glow with bioluminescent plankton at night. Wade in the shallow water at the shoreline after dark for a magical, free, and unforgettable romantic experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely guesthouse breakfast – full spread with tropical fruits, eggs, and fresh juice (MVR 80–120)
meals.lunch: Local café lunch – try saagu bondibai (sago pudding) for dessert (MVR 70–110)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the guesthouse if kitchen is available, or enjoy a budget local restaurant dinner (MVR 90–150)

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescence is best viewed during new moon phases when skies are darkest. Check the lunar calendar for your trip dates. Even without bioluminescence, a nighttime beach walk under the stars in the Maldives is extraordinarily romantic.

day_by_day.morning: Beginner scuba diving discovery dive or snorkeling with a marine biologist guide – many budget dive centers in North Malé Atoll offer discover scuba sessions for $60–80 per person. This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience for non-divers wanting to explore the underwater world more deeply.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the dive, relax and rehydrate. Visit the guesthouse or nearby café for a light meal. Spend the afternoon reviewing your underwater photos and planning the remaining days.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset fishing trip – join a traditional Maldivian hand-line fishing excursion at sunset ($15–25 per person). Try your luck catching your own dinner! Many operators will cook your catch for you back at the guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-dive breakfast – toast, banana, and water (avoid heavy meals before diving) (MVR 40–60)
meals.lunch: Post-dive recovery meal at local café – rice, curry, and fresh lime juice (MVR 90–140)
meals.dinner: Your freshly caught fish grilled or cooked by the guesthouse chef – a truly special and budget-friendly dinner experience (MVR 50–100 cooking fee)

day_by_day.notes: Divers must wait at least 12–18 hours after diving before flying. Plan dive days accordingly relative to your departure date. The discovery dive is perfect for honeymoon couples wanting to try something adventurous together for the first time.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Malé city – take the public ferry from North Malé Atoll to the capital city (MVR 10–15). Explore the colorful streets of Malé, visit the Grand Friday Mosque (Masjid al-Sultan Muhammad Thakurufaanu Al Auzam), and the Old Friday Mosque (Hukuru Miskiy) with its intricate coral stone carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Maldives in Sultan Park (entry MVR 100 for foreigners) to learn about the history and royal heritage of the islands. Explore the local fish market and produce market for a vibrant, authentic local experience.
day_by_day.evening: Browse the local shops along Majeedhee Magu (Malé's main shopping street) for budget souvenirs. Return to your guesthouse by public ferry before sunset.

meals.breakfast: Local Malé café breakfast – roshi and mas huni with hot tea (MVR 40–70)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Malé restaurant – rice, curry, and fresh fish (MVR 60–100). Try one of the many local 'short eats' cafés for an authentic experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner back near your guesthouse – grilled tuna steak at a local eatery (MVR 120–170)

day_by_day.notes: Malé is one of the world's most densely populated cities and is a fascinating contrast to the tranquil resort islands. The fish market is most lively in the early morning. Dress modestly when visiting mosques and religious sites.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling with whale sharks or manta rays – North Malé Atoll is one of the best places in the world to snorkel with these gentle giants. Book a specialized shared group excursion ($40–60 per person). Best seasons vary but March can be excellent for mantas around cleaning stations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from excursion and enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the beach. Try stand-up paddleboarding or simply float in the crystal-clear lagoon. Enjoy the post-excursion high of swimming with the ocean's largest fish.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic private beach dinner setup – ask your guesthouse in advance to arrange a simple candlelit beach dinner (many budget guesthouses can arrange this for $30–60 extra). Enjoy the stars and the sound of the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast – eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee (MVR 70–100)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the excursion boat or stop at local island café (MVR 70–110)
meals.dinner: Special private candlelit beach dinner arranged through guesthouse – a budget-romantic splurge for your honeymoon (MVR 400–600 per couple for the setup and meal)

day_by_day.notes: Whale shark encounters are subject to seasonal patterns and ocean conditions. Your operator will know the best current spots. This is arguably the most breathtaking wildlife experience the Maldives offers and is highly recommended for couples.

day_by_day.morning: Underwater photography or snorkel photography session – rent an underwater camera from your guesthouse or local dive shop ($15–25 for the day) and spend the morning capturing memories of the house reef. Create your own romantic underwater photo album.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hulhumalé – the newly developed reclaimed island near the airport. Explore its wide beaches, bicycle-friendly paths, and modern local cafés. Hulhumalé has a relaxed, less touristy vibe and beautiful long stretches of beach.
day_by_day.evening: Final shopping and souvenir buying evening. Visit local craft shops for lacquerware boxes, thundu kunaa (woven mats), and Maldivian jewelry. Pack thoughtfully to stay within airline baggage limits.

meals.breakfast: Local café breakfast – pancakes with coconut syrup and fresh juice (MVR 60–90)
meals.lunch: Hulhumalé café lunch – try a modern Maldivian fusion café for a slightly different experience (MVR 80–130)
meals.dinner: Farewell-style dinner at your favorite local restaurant discovered during the trip (MVR 150–220)

day_by_day.notes: Hulhumalé is accessible by ferry from Malé and is very budget-friendly to visit. The beaches here are less crowded than resort islands. If you want one final snorkel, the waters around Hulhumalé also have decent reef areas.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise swim and snorkel from the house reef. Take one last long swim in the turquoise lagoon and say goodbye to the underwater world. Collect a few photos and soak in the beauty of your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out preparation and packing. Settle any outstanding bills with your guesthouse. Take a final walk around the local island to say goodbye to any friendly locals you've met during your stay.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final evening – sit on the beach, watch the sunset, reflect on your 13-day Maldivian adventure, and enjoy a special farewell dinner. Exchange travel stories and memories.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast – enjoy a full meal as you may not eat again until the airport (MVR 80–120)
meals.lunch: Light local lunch – short eats and fresh coconut water (MVR 50–80)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered – treat yourselves to a slightly nicer meal to celebrate your honeymoon trip (MVR 250–400 per couple)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some MVR cash for final tips to guesthouse staff who have made your stay special. Tipping is appreciated but not mandatory. Ensure all your snorkel gear, underwater camera rentals, and equipment are returned before check-out.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning leisure – depending on your departure flight time, enjoy one last breakfast and a walk on the beach. Begin transfer to Velana International Airport. Allow extra time for the ferry transfer from North Malé Atoll (typically 20–45 minutes depending on your exact location).
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport check-in and departure procedures. Browse the duty-free shops at Velana International Airport for any last-minute gifts. Enjoy a final Maldivian meal at the airport if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Depart the Maldives with extraordinary memories of your budget honeymoon paradise. Carry home the warmth of the Indian Ocean, the magic of the coral reefs, and the romance of the most beautiful archipelago on earth.

meals.breakfast: Final guesthouse breakfast or early café stop before transfer (MVR 60–100)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café – budget meal before departure (MVR 100–180 or airport prices)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at your layover destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. The ferry from North Malé Atoll to the airport island is straightforward – confirm schedules the night before. Declare any coral, shells, or marine souvenirs if required by customs. Most natural items cannot be exported legally from the Maldives.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00 at Velana International Airport (Malé)
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Velana International Airport at 13:00. Complete immigration and customs formalities. Transfer by speedboat (~20–40 min) to your boutique resort in North Malé Atoll near Veligandu or Baros Island. Check in, unpack, and settle into your overwater or beach villa. Enjoy a welcome drink and explore the resort grounds at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the resort's private beach at sunset to soak in your first Maldivian evening. Enjoy a romantic welcome dinner at the resort's main restaurant — opt for the fresh catch of the day or a Maldivian fish curry to start your culinary journey.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at Velana International Airport or upon arrival at the resort's welcome lounge
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant — fresh seafood platter or Maldivian fish curry with coconut rice (mid-range set menu, approx. $40–$60 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Request an early check-in if possible when booking. Confirm your speedboat transfer details with the resort in advance. Keep Day 1 relaxed — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Exchange some currency to Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR) at the airport for local island tips.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy your first sunrise over the Indian Ocean from your villa deck. After breakfast, head to the resort's house reef for a self-guided introductory snorkel session. Explore the vibrant coral gardens just steps from the beach — spot parrotfish, butterflyfish, and perhaps a friendly reef shark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the resort's guided house reef snorkeling tour (usually complimentary or low-cost through the dive center). The guide will point out sea turtles, moray eels, and colorful reef fish. Return to the villa for a midday rest and enjoy the resort pool with a refreshing mocktail or cocktail.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne — embark on a traditional Maldivian wooden dhoni boat chartered exclusively for two, sailing through the turquoise lagoon as the sun dips below the horizon. Toast with chilled champagne and canapés while watching the sky turn gold and pink.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet at the beachside restaurant — tropical fruits, eggs, pastries, fresh juices (included or approx. $20–$30 pp)
meals.lunch: Resort beach grill — grilled fish sandwich, fresh salad, and coconut water (approx. $20–$35 pp)
meals.dinner: Light dinner back at the resort after the dhoni cruise — tapas-style sharing plates at the bar lounge or resort bistro (approx. $35–$55 pp)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with the resort concierge as early as possible — it is one of the most popular romantic experiences and slots fill quickly. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and an underwater camera or GoPro for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast, prepare for a half-day Coral Reef Snorkeling Safari at Hanifaru Bay — a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in Baa Atoll renowned for its spectacular aggregations of manta rays and whale sharks. Depart by speedboat with a certified guide (note: Hanifaru Bay requires a day trip from North Malé Atoll, approximately 1.5–2 hours each way — confirm logistics with your resort).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hanifaru Bay and snorkel in the protected marine sanctuary. Witness manta rays gliding effortlessly through plankton-rich waters — an utterly magical and romantic experience. The guide will brief you on responsible snorkeling etiquette to protect the ecosystem. Return journey by speedboat in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Freshen up and enjoy a quiet, intimate dinner for two on the resort's overwater deck or beach — request a private table setup with candles and lanterns for a romantic ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — full spread with local and international options
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch provided by the resort or tour operator on the boat — sandwiches, fruit, snacks, and water
meals.dinner: Resort overwater or beachside restaurant — grilled lobster or snapper with sautéed vegetables and a bottle of house wine (approx. $50–$75 pp)

day_by_day.notes: Hanifaru Bay snorkeling safaris are best between May and November when manta rays are most abundant; in March, sightings are possible but less guaranteed — ask your resort about current marine conditions. The trip is a full-day excursion so wear comfortable, sun-protective clothing. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Entry to Hanifaru Bay requires a conservation fee (~$15 USD pp).

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow, indulgent morning — sleep in, have breakfast in bed (request in-villa dining the night before), and lounge on your private terrace or overwater deck. Take a morning dip in the lagoon and simply breathe in the tranquility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Treat yourselves to the Underwater Spa Treatment — indulge in a signature couples massage at an overwater or semi-submerged spa pavilion with a glass floor, allowing you to watch tropical fish glide beneath you as you relax. This deeply romantic and luxurious experience is the highlight of many Maldives honeymoons. Session typically lasts 60–90 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: After the spa, unwind in the resort's infinity pool as the sun sets. Dress up for a special dinner at the resort's premium à la carte restaurant — the perfect end to a deeply relaxing day.

meals.breakfast: In-villa dining — continental breakfast with fresh fruits, yogurt, pastries, and coffee/tea delivered to your terrace
meals.lunch: Resort pool bar — light bites such as bruschetta, fish tacos, and fresh coconut (approx. $25–$40 pp)
meals.dinner: Resort à la carte fine-dining restaurant — tasting menu with Maldivian-inspired dishes, fresh seafood, and dessert (approx. $60–$90 pp with wine pairing)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Underwater Spa Treatment well in advance — spa slots are limited and honeymoon packages may include discounts. Opt for the 'Maldivian Drift' or 'Ocean Harmony' couples treatment if available. Arrive 15 minutes early to enjoy the spa's relaxation lounge and herbal teas.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise kayaking session around the resort's lagoon — most resorts offer complimentary kayak rentals. Paddle through calm, crystal-clear waters as the sky lights up in shades of orange and pink. Return for a hearty breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Private Sandbank Picnic Dining Experience — be whisked away by speedboat to a secluded, uninhabited white sandbank in the middle of the Indian Ocean. A dedicated resort butler will have set up a beautifully styled picnic with fresh food, chilled drinks, and a hammock or sun loungers. Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and enjoying complete privacy in paradise.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a casual, relaxed evening — browse the resort's boutique for local crafts or souvenirs, then have a laid-back dinner at the resort's casual beachside eatery.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — eggs made to order, fresh tropical fruits, smoothies, and local Maldivian breakfast items like mas huni (tuna and coconut)
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper on the sandbank — artisan sandwiches, charcuterie, tropical fruits, sparkling water, and champagne or mocktails (included in sandbank experience, approx. $80–$120 pp)
meals.dinner: Resort casual beachside restaurant — wood-fired pizza, pasta, or grilled fish with a glass of wine (approx. $30–$50 pp)

day_by_day.notes: The Private Sandbank Picnic must be booked at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Bring extra sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses as there is no shade on the sandbank. The experience typically lasts 3–4 hours. Tide conditions affect sandbank availability — the concierge will confirm timing.

day_by_day.morning: Join the resort's guided morning snorkeling trip to a nearby coral pinnacle or outer reef channel — different from the house reef, these excursions often yield sightings of reef sharks, eagle rays, and large schools of fish. Depart by resort dhoni at around 8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by midday and enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the resort. Lounge by the pool, read a book, or try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) in the lagoon — a fun and surprisingly peaceful activity for couples.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Maldivian cultural evening at the resort (many resorts host weekly Bodu Beru drumming and dance performances by local artists). Enjoy cocktails and light bites while watching the vibrant performance under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — early start to prepare for the morning snorkel trip
meals.lunch: Resort pool bar or beach grill — grilled corn, fish skewers, fresh juices, and a shared mezze platter (approx. $25–$40 pp)
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant during the cultural evening — buffet-style Maldivian and international spread with live entertainment (approx. $40–$60 pp)

day_by_day.notes: Ask the dive center about the best snorkeling sites accessible from your resort — staff will know current conditions and visibility. SUP boards and kayaks are often included in the room rate or available for a nominal fee. Check the resort's weekly activity schedule upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate this morning to a Maldivian Cultural Village Tour & Traditional Cooking Class. Take a short speedboat ride to the inhabited local island of Maafushi or a nearby local island to explore authentic Maldivian culture. Walk through narrow streets lined with colorful homes, visit the local mosque, and browse small shops selling handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a hands-on traditional cooking class led by a local Maldivian family or cooking instructor. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as garudhiya (tuna broth), mas huni, rihaakuru (fish paste), and coconut-based curries. Enjoy your freshly cooked meal together as lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Spend the evening stargazing from your villa deck or the resort's beach — the Maldives offers some of the most spectacular night skies in the world due to minimal light pollution. Many resorts offer guided stargazing sessions.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — fuel up before the cultural excursion
meals.lunch: Maldivian home-cooked meal prepared during the cooking class on the local island — garudhiya, mas huni, roshi (flatbread), and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — light dinner of sushi, sashimi, or a fresh seafood salad (approx. $30–$50 pp)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting local islands — shoulders and knees should be covered out of respect for local customs. Bikinis and swimwear are not permitted in local island villages. Bring cash (USD or MVR) for purchasing local crafts. The cooking class can be arranged through the resort or directly with local island tour operators.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a completely free and unstructured morning — this is your mid-trip recovery day. Sleep in, have breakfast at your own pace, and simply do whatever feels right. Float in the lagoon, read by the pool, or just sit on your terrace and listen to the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the resort's marine biology center or coral restoration program (available at many Maldivian resorts). Learn about the fragile coral ecosystem, participate in a coral planting activity, and adopt a coral fragment as a meaningful honeymoon memento.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a romantic Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise (second experience or a variation such as a dolphin-watching cruise if available). Many resorts offer dolphin-spotting excursions at dusk when spinner dolphins are active in the channels.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast — order your favorites from the room service menu and enjoy on the terrace
meals.lunch: Resort beach club — light, healthy options such as grain bowls, avocado toast, fresh juices, and smoothie bowls (approx. $20–$35 pp)
meals.dinner: Resort overwater restaurant — Mediterranean-inspired menu with fresh seafood, olive oil, herbs, and a crisp white wine (approx. $45–$65 pp)

day_by_day.notes: The coral planting activity is a deeply meaningful and educational experience — many couples treasure the certificate and GPS coordinates of their planted coral. Ask the resort's marine biologist about the health of the local reef and how climate change is affecting it. Dolphin sightings are common in the Maldives but not guaranteed.

day_by_day.morning: Take an introductory scuba diving lesson (Discover Scuba Diving / DSD) with the resort's PADI-certified dive center if you are not already certified. This beginner-friendly experience takes place in the shallow lagoon and allows you to explore the underwater world at depth for the first time — an unforgettable shared experience for couples.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the dive, enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the resort's spa — book individual treatments such as a Maldivian coconut scrub, hot stone massage, or reflexology session. Many resorts offer half-day spa packages at discounted rates.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a candlelit beach dinner — request a private table set up directly on the sand with lanterns, flowers, and a personalized menu. This is one of the most romantic dining experiences the Maldives has to offer.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — light breakfast before the morning dive session
meals.lunch: Resort dive center café or poolside bar — energy-boosting post-dive meal with grilled chicken, rice, salad, and fresh juice (approx. $25–$40 pp)
meals.dinner: Private beach candlelit dinner — set menu of 3–4 courses including lobster bisque, grilled reef fish, and chocolate fondant for dessert, with a bottle of sparkling wine (approx. $80–$120 pp — a worthwhile splurge)

day_by_day.notes: The introductory dive does not require any prior experience — the instructor will guide you through everything in the water. Inform the dive instructor of any medical conditions beforehand. Book the private beach dinner at least 2 days in advance and specify any dietary requirements or special requests (rose petals, honeymoon cake, etc.).

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling at a different reef site — ask the dive center about a boat snorkel trip to a nearby thilas (submerged reef pinnacles) or channel known for strong currents and large pelagic fish. These sites often yield sightings of hammerhead sharks, eagle rays, and large tuna.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and spend the afternoon on a glass-bottom kayak tour of the lagoon — a unique and peaceful way to observe the underwater world without getting wet. Alternatively, enjoy a guided lagoon photography session with an underwater camera provided by the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private in-villa movie night — many resorts offer an outdoor cinema setup with a projector screen, bean bags, popcorn, and blankets on the beach or villa deck. Request your favorite romantic film and enjoy a cozy evening under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — early start for the morning boat snorkel
meals.lunch: On-boat packed lunch or return to resort for a beach grill lunch — fish burgers, fries, and tropical fruit salad (approx. $25–$40 pp)
meals.dinner: In-villa dining — romantic room service dinner with a curated 3-course menu and a bottle of wine enjoyed on your private terrace (approx. $50–$80 pp)

day_by_day.notes: Channel and thila snorkeling involves stronger currents and is more suitable for confident swimmers — discuss your comfort level with the dive center beforehand. The private movie night setup typically costs $50–$100 and should be arranged through the concierge. This is a wonderful low-key evening after several activity-packed days.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate this morning to a leisurely resort exploration — visit the resort's boutique, write postcards, or simply walk the full perimeter of the island (most Maldivian resort islands can be walked in 15–20 minutes). Enjoy a slow breakfast and coffee on your terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided big game fishing excursion with the resort's fishing team — try your hand at trolling for yellowfin tuna, wahoo, or mahi-mahi in the deep blue waters beyond the reef. No experience necessary. Catch-and-release is encouraged, though some resorts will prepare your catch for dinner.
day_by_day.evening: If you caught a fish, have the resort chef prepare it as your dinner — a truly farm-to-table (or ocean-to-table) experience. Enjoy it at the resort's main restaurant with a glass of chilled white wine and a side of roasted vegetables.

meals.breakfast: In-villa continental breakfast — croissants, jam, fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the fishing boat — sandwiches, snacks, and cold drinks provided by the resort
meals.dinner: Resort main restaurant — your fresh catch prepared by the chef (grilled, pan-seared, or in a curry) with sides and wine (approx. $40–$60 pp including the fish preparation fee)

day_by_day.notes: The fishing excursion typically lasts 3–4 hours in the afternoon and costs $80–$150 per couple depending on the resort. Wear a hat and sunscreen as sun exposure on the open water is intense. If fishing is not of interest, substitute with a snorkeling trip to a new reef site or a relaxing afternoon at the spa.

day_by_day.morning: Your second-to-last full day — make the most of it with a morning yoga or meditation session on the beach or your villa deck. Many resorts offer complimentary sunrise yoga classes led by an instructor. Start the day with intention and gratitude for this incredible journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon doing your favorite activities from the trip — whether that's snorkeling the house reef one last time, lounging by the pool, or simply floating in the lagoon. Visit the resort gift shop to pick up meaningful souvenirs such as local crafts, Maldivian black coral jewelry, or resort-branded keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your final full evening with a special honeymoon dinner — return to your favorite restaurant from the trip or try the resort's most premium dining option. Request a honeymoon dessert platter or a personalized cake to mark the occasion.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — indulge in everything you love one last time
meals.lunch: Resort pool bar — shared platters of mezze, fresh fruit, and cocktails (approx. $30–$45 pp)
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — honeymoon celebration dinner with a chef's tasting menu, wine pairing, and a personalized dessert (approx. $80–$120 pp — your final special splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Ask the resort to arrange a honeymoon turndown service for your final night — rose petals, candles, and a personalized card are a lovely touch. This is also a good evening to settle your resort bill and confirm departure logistics for the next morning. Pack non-essentials tonight to make the morning smoother.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up for one final sunrise over the Indian Ocean — take photos and soak in every last moment. Enjoy a final breakfast at the resort. Take a last swim in the lagoon or a walk along the beach to say goodbye to your paradise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort and transfer by speedboat back to Velana International Airport in Malé. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the transfer, check-in, and security. Browse the duty-free shops at the airport for last-minute gifts — Maldivian vanilla, local honey, and resort-branded items make wonderful souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Velana International Airport, carrying with you memories of 13 magical days in the Maldives — a honeymoon that will last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy your favorites and take your time
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Velana International Airport — light meal before your flight (approx. $15–$25 pp)
meals.dinner: On the flight home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your speedboat transfer time with the resort the evening before departure — transfers to the airport must be timed carefully to avoid missing your flight. Keep a small bag with travel essentials easily accessible during the transfer. Carry any fragile souvenirs in your carry-on luggage. Most importantly — treasure every moment of this journey together.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Maldives Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: North Malé Atoll, near Veligandu or Baros Island Boutique Stay
hotel.location: North Malé Atoll, near Veligandu or Baros Island

experiences.name: Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne
experiences.description: Embark on a traditional Maldivian wooden dhoni boat chartered exclusively for two, sailing through turquoise lagoons as the sun dips below the horizon. Enjoy chilled champagne, fresh tropical fruit platters, and a private butler while dolphins often accompany the vessel. A quintessential romantic experience perfectly suited for honeymooners seeking intimacy and natural beauty.
experiences.location: North Malé Atoll, near Veligandu or Baros Island

experiences.name: Coral Reef Snorkeling Safari at Hanifaru Bay
experiences.description: Join a guided snorkeling safari to Hanifaru Bay, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve renowned for its spectacular congregation of manta rays and whale sharks. Glide through crystal-clear waters teeming with vibrant coral gardens, sea turtles, and exotic reef fish. A small-group guided tour ensures an intimate, eco-conscious experience that is both thrilling and unforgettable for snorkeling enthusiasts.

experiences.name: Underwater Spa Treatment
experiences.description: Indulge in a signature couples massage at an overwater or semi-submerged spa pavilion with a glass floor, allowing you to watch colorful marine life drift beneath you as skilled therapists perform traditional Maldivian healing rituals using coconut oil and local botanicals. This ultra-luxurious experience blends wellness, romance, and the mesmerizing underwater world into one serene session.
experiences.location: Rangali Island, South Ari Atoll (Conrad Maldives area)

experiences.name: Private Sandbank Picnic Dining Experience
experiences.description: Be whisked away by speedboat to a secluded, uninhabited white sandbank in the middle of the Indian Ocean, where a personal chef and butler set up a gourmet candlelit picnic just for two. Savor freshly grilled Maldivian lobster, sashimi-grade tuna, tropical salads, and artisan desserts while surrounded by nothing but endless blue ocean and sky — the ultimate honeymoon memory.

experiences.name: Maldivian Cultural Village Tour & Traditional Cooking Class
experiences.description: Visit the inhabited local island of Maafushi or Hulhumalé to explore authentic Maldivian culture, including a guided walk through a traditional fishing village, a visit to a historic mosque, and a hands-on cooking class where a local family teaches you to prepare classic dishes like mas huni (tuna and coconut), garudhiya fish broth, and sweet bondibai rice pudding. A meaningful cultural immersion that complements the luxury resort experience.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Malé Velana International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and collect luggage. Meet your private resort transfer coordinator and board a luxury speedboat or seaplane transfer to your boutique resort near Veligandu or Baros Island in North Malé Atoll (approx. 20–45 min). Check in to your overwater villa, receive a welcome drink with fresh coconut water and tropical flowers, and take a leisurely orientation tour of the resort with your personal butler.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your villa and enjoy the private deck as the sun begins to set over the Indian Ocean. Head to the resort's signature overwater restaurant for a romantic welcome dinner featuring fresh Maldivian lobster, grilled reef fish, and a curated wine pairing. Toast to the beginning of your honeymoon journey.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack and tropical fruit platter arranged by the resort upon arrival in your villa
meals.dinner: Romantic dinner at the resort's premier overwater restaurant — recommended: Maldivian lobster thermidor, seared yellowfin tuna, and a bottle of Moët & Chandon Champagne

day_by_day.notes: Request early villa preparation with the resort in advance. Ask your butler to arrange rose petal turndown service and a honeymoon welcome amenity (sparkling wine, chocolates, flower bath). Confirm seaplane or speedboat transfer timing ahead of landing.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up to a private in-villa floating breakfast delivered by your butler — fresh tropical fruits, pastries, eggs to order, fresh juices, and coffee served on your overwater deck. Spend the morning at leisure exploring the house reef directly from your villa steps. Snorkel among vibrant coral gardens, sea turtles, and reef sharks in the crystal-clear lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the resort's overwater spa for the Underwater Spa Treatment — a signature couples massage in a semi-submerged glass-floor spa pavilion. Watch colorful fish glide beneath you as skilled therapists perform a 90-minute Balinese-Maldivian fusion massage using warm coconut and frangipani oils. Follow with a dip in the couples' hydrotherapy pool.
day_by_day.evening: Change into resort-chic attire and enjoy sundowner cocktails at the beachside bar as the sky turns gold and crimson. Dine at the resort's beach grill restaurant with feet in the sand — choose from a freshly caught seafood platter, grilled octopus, and Maldivian curry with roshi bread.

meals.breakfast: In-villa floating breakfast on your overwater deck — tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, fresh juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's pool bar — grilled reef fish tacos, fresh ceviche, and a chilled coconut
meals.dinner: Barefoot beach grill dinner — whole grilled lobster, Maldivian fish curry, and a chilled Sancerre white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Underwater Spa Treatment at least 2 days in advance as couples slots fill quickly. Ask the spa to prepare a post-massage Champagne and fruit platter on your villa deck. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast on your villa deck, gear up for a guided house reef snorkeling session with the resort's marine biologist. Discover the micro-ecosystems of the coral garden — spot nudibranchs, moray eels, octopuses, and schools of fusiliers. The marine biologist will provide fascinating insights into the reef's biodiversity and conservation efforts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a private speedboat for the Private Sandbank Picnic Dining Experience. Be whisked to a secluded uninhabited sandbank surrounded by turquoise water in every direction. Your butler and a private chef will have pre-arranged a luxury picnic setup — a canopied daybed, chilled Champagne on ice, a gourmet spread of charcuterie, sushi, fresh fruits, and desserts. Swim, snorkel, and sunbathe in total privacy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort refreshed. Enjoy a quiet evening with a private stargazing session arranged on your villa's sun deck — the resort's astronomer provides a telescope and guided tour of the Maldivian night sky. End the night with a nightcap of aged rum cocktails in your villa.

meals.breakfast: À la carte resort breakfast at the main restaurant — eggs your way, smoked salmon bagel, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet private sandbank picnic — Champagne, sushi platter, charcuterie board, tropical fruits, and macarons
meals.dinner: In-villa private dining — your butler serves a 4-course set menu featuring Maldivian reef fish soup, lobster bisque, grilled snapper, and passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: The sandbank excursion is weather-dependent; confirm the morning of departure. Bring a hat, reef-safe sunscreen, and a light cover-up for the sandbank. The stargazing experience is best requested during new moon phases — check the lunar calendar.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a sunrise yoga session on your private villa deck or the resort's overwater yoga platform, led by the resident yoga instructor. The gentle sound of lapping waves and the pastel dawn sky create a deeply meditative atmosphere. Follow with a nourishing açaí bowl and herbal tea breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Coral Reef Snorkeling Safari at Hanifaru Bay — a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and one of the world's most extraordinary marine sites. Board a private or small-group guided boat to Hanifaru Bay (in Baa Atoll — coordinate with resort for day trip logistics). Snorkel alongside manta rays and whale sharks in their natural feeding aggregation grounds. A certified marine guide accompanies you throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in the late afternoon, glowing from an extraordinary day. Freshen up and head to the resort's wine cellar lounge for a private wine and cheese tasting curated by the sommelier. Retire for a romantic candlelit dinner on your villa's overwater deck under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Light wellness breakfast — açaí bowl, chia pudding, matcha latte, and tropical fruit platter
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet bento box on the boat — sandwiches, fresh fruit, energy bars, and chilled water (arranged by resort)
meals.dinner: Private candlelit overwater deck dinner — pan-seared grouper, truffle risotto, and a decadent chocolate lava cake with vanilla bean ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Hanifaru Bay is in Baa Atoll, which requires a seaplane or domestic flight from North Malé Atoll — confirm day-trip logistics and permits with the resort concierge at least 3 days in advance. Manta ray season peaks March–November. No flash photography or touching marine life.

day_by_day.morning: A slower, indulgent morning — sleep in and enjoy breakfast in bed arranged by your butler with freshly baked croissants, fruit, and coffee. Spend the mid-morning reading, relaxing in your private plunge pool, or enjoying a gentle swim in the lagoon. Optionally, take a stand-up paddleboarding lesson with the resort's water sports team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Maldivian Cultural Village Tour & Traditional Cooking Class. Board a speedboat to the nearby inhabited local island of Maafushi or a similar local island accessible from North Malé Atoll. Explore the island on foot — visit the Friday Mosque, the local cemetery with coral stone carvings, and the bustling harbor. Then participate in a hands-on traditional Maldivian cooking class: learn to prepare mas huni (tuna and coconut salad), garudhiya (fish broth), and bondi (sweet rice cakes).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and unwind. Treat yourselves to the resort's signature sundowner ritual — a private beach bonfire with roasted marshmallows, cocktails, and soft background music arranged by your butler. Watch the stars emerge over the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in bed — freshly baked croissants, tropical fruit, yogurt parfait, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional Maldivian lunch on the local island as part of the cooking class — mas huni, roshi, hedhikaa snacks, and fresh lime juice
meals.dinner: Resort's main restaurant — a curated tasting menu with Maldivian-French fusion cuisine, paired with a sommelier-selected wine flight

day_by_day.notes: When visiting local islands, dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) out of respect for the local Muslim culture. Bring small gifts or support local artisans by purchasing handmade lacquerwork or woven mats. The cooking class is typically 2–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided dolphin-watching cruise departing at dawn. North Malé Atoll is home to large pods of spinner dolphins that leap and play in the bow waves of boats at sunrise. Your private boat glides silently through the glassy morning sea as dolphins dance around you — a truly magical experience for couples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return for a late resort breakfast, then spend the afternoon at the resort's overwater infinity pool with personalized cocktail service. Arrange for a couples' in-villa spa treatment — a traditional Maldivian herbal scrub and hot stone massage performed by the resort's in-villa spa therapists on your private deck.
day_by_day.evening: This evening, embark on the Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise with Champagne. Board a beautifully decorated traditional wooden dhoni chartered exclusively for two. Sail through the shimmering golden waters as the sun melts into the horizon. Sip chilled Champagne, enjoy canapés, and watch the sky transform into shades of amber, rose, and violet. A truly unforgettable romantic experience.

meals.breakfast: Post-dolphin cruise brunch at the resort — eggs Florentine, smoked salmon, fresh juices, and a Bloody Mary
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — tuna tartare, avocado toast, and a chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Late dinner back at the resort after the dhoni cruise — grilled Maldivian jumbo prawns, coconut curry, and a shared dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: The dolphin cruise departs very early (around 6:00–6:30 AM) — arrange a light packed breakfast with your butler the evening before. The sunset dhoni cruise typically lasts 1.5–2 hours; confirm the departure time based on sunset (around 18:15–18:30 in March). Bring a light wrap for the sea breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint of your journey — celebrate with a special mid-trip morning. Request the resort to prepare a flower-strewn private beach setup for a slow champagne brunch on the sand. Spend the morning swimming in the lagoon and enjoying the resort's non-motorized water sports — kayaking and snorkeling along the outer reef edge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private scuba diving introductory session (Discover Scuba Diving) with the resort's PADI-certified dive center if you haven't dived before, or a guided two-tank dive to a nearby wreck or coral pinnacle if you're certified. North Malé Atoll offers world-class dive sites including Banana Reef, HP Reef, and Manta Point.
day_by_day.evening: A deeply romantic evening — your butler arranges a private overwater dining table suspended above the lagoon, lit with lanterns and candles. A dedicated private chef prepares a bespoke 5-course dinner just for the two of you, with live acoustic guitar music softly playing in the background.

meals.breakfast: Private beach Champagne brunch — smoked salmon, oysters, pastries, eggs station, and tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Post-dive light lunch at the dive center's café — fresh wraps, fruit smoothies, and energy bars
meals.dinner: Exclusive private overwater 5-course dinner — amuse-bouche, lobster bisque, seared scallops, prime beef tenderloin, and a chocolate and raspberry mille-feuille with Champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the private overwater dinner setup at least 3 days in advance — it is one of the resort's most sought-after experiences. For scuba diving, bring your certification card if certified. Non-swimmers can enjoy snorkeling with flotation aids instead.

day_by_day.morning: A full wellness morning — begin with a guided meditation session on the beach at sunrise, followed by a resort-led aqua yoga class in the shallow lagoon. The warm, waist-deep water and gentle current create a uniquely calming yoga experience. Afterward, enjoy a nutritious smoothie bowl and herbal infusions at the wellness café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the resort's marine conservation program — join the resident marine biologist for a coral planting workshop. Plant your own coral fragment on the resort's reef restoration frame and receive a personalized certificate. You can track your coral's growth online after returning home — a meaningful and lasting honeymoon memory.
day_by_day.evening: Dress up for a special evening at the resort's premium sushi and sake bar (or Japanese-inspired restaurant if available). Enjoy an omakase-style tasting menu with premium sashimi, nigiri, and sake pairings. End the night with a moonlit walk along the resort's private beach.

meals.breakfast: Wellness café breakfast — açaí smoothie bowl, green juice, overnight oats with mango, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: In-villa lunch on the deck — grilled reef fish, quinoa salad, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Resort's Japanese-inspired restaurant — omakase sushi and sashimi tasting menu with premium sake and Japanese whisky pairing

day_by_day.notes: The coral planting workshop is typically offered in the afternoon and lasts about 1 hour. Wear water shoes and a rash guard. Ask the marine biologist about the resort's broader reef conservation initiatives — many luxury resorts in the Maldives are deeply committed to sustainability.

day_by_day.morning: An adventurous morning — rent a private catamaran or sailing yacht through the resort's water sports center for a half-day private sailing excursion around the atoll. Sail to a remote uninhabited island, drop anchor, and snorkel the surrounding reef. Your captain will bring a cooler with chilled drinks and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a long, indulgent afternoon at the spa. Book the resort's premium Royal Couple's Ritual — a 3-hour journey including a full-body exfoliation with Maldivian sea salt and coconut, a deep-tissue couples massage, a floral milk bath, and a facial using marine-derived ingredients. Pure bliss.
day_by_day.evening: A low-key, intimate evening — pick up a bottle of fine wine from the resort's cellar and enjoy a private sunset on your villa deck with a charcuterie and cheese board prepared by the kitchen. Watch the bioluminescent plankton glow in the waves below your overwater villa as night falls.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant breakfast — eggs your way, freshly baked bread, cold cuts, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: On the catamaran — gourmet picnic prepared by the resort chef: baguettes, charcuterie, grapes, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Casual in-villa dining — artisan cheese and charcuterie board, crusty bread, and a bottle of fine Burgundy red wine

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescent plankton is most visible on very dark nights away from artificial light — turn off your villa lights and look into the water from your deck. The phenomenon is more pronounced in warmer months. Ask the resort team if conditions are favorable.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a completely unstructured, blissful morning. Order an extravagant in-villa brunch — eggs Benedict with truffle hollandaise, smoked salmon, Champagne mimosas, and a decadent pastry basket. Lounge in your private plunge pool, read, and simply exist in paradise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided big-game fishing excursion (half-day) aboard a private sport fishing vessel. The waters around North Malé Atoll are rich with yellowfin tuna, dorado, and wahoo. Whether you catch something or not, the experience of deep-sea fishing in the open Indian Ocean is exhilarating. Arrange for your catch to be prepared by the resort chef for dinner.
day_by_day.evening: The resort chef prepares your freshly caught fish in your preferred style — grilled with lemon butter, sashimi-style, or as a Maldivian curry. Dine on your villa deck as your personal butler serves the meal course by course under the stars. A truly farm-to-table (or ocean-to-table) honeymoon dinner.

meals.breakfast: Extravagant in-villa brunch — eggs Benedict with truffle hollandaise, Champagne mimosas, smoked salmon, and pastry basket
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the fishing boat — sandwiches, fresh fruit, energy drinks, and cold water
meals.dinner: Ocean-to-table private villa dinner — your freshly caught fish prepared by the resort chef, served with sautéed vegetables, coconut rice, and a chilled Chablis

day_by_day.notes: Confirm fishing excursion availability and species regulations with the resort — catch-and-release is encouraged for larger species. Bring motion sickness medication if you're sensitive to ocean swells. The resort's chef will need advance notice to prepare your catch for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: An early morning snorkeling safari to a nearby drift snorkel site — the resort's dive team takes you to a channel where the current carries you effortlessly past walls of coral, eagle rays, reef sharks, and turtles. A thrilling and effortless way to experience the reef's abundance. Return for a late breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dedicate the afternoon to pure resort luxury — reserve a private cabana at the overwater pool, order a customized cocktail menu, and enjoy personalized service from the pool butler. Optionally, participate in a private mixology class where the resort's head bartender teaches you to craft traditional Maldivian-inspired cocktails using local ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Your penultimate full evening — make it memorable with a second Private Sunset Dhoni Cruise or alternatively a private beach dinner with a bonfire, lanterns, and a live Maldivian traditional music and bodu beru drum performance arranged exclusively for the two of you.

meals.breakfast: Post-snorkel resort breakfast — tropical fruit platter, granola and yogurt, smoked fish, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Private poolside cabana lunch — lobster roll, fresh ceviche, truffle fries, and a chilled rosé spritz
meals.dinner: Private beach bonfire dinner — grilled whole snapper, Maldivian reef lobster, coconut dessert, and a Champagne toast under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The bodu beru performance is a traditional Maldivian drumming and dance ceremony — a deeply cultural and festive experience. Arrange this through the resort concierge at least 3 days in advance. Tip the performers generously as a gesture of appreciation.

day_by_day.morning: Your final full day — begin it with a sunrise snorkeling session at the house reef, savoring every last moment beneath the surface. Watch the reef wake up as the morning light filters through the water and illuminates the coral. Return for a long, leisurely breakfast at the main restaurant.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on a final indulgent villa retreat — arrange a couples' hammam experience in your villa, followed by a private photo session with the resort's underwater photographer in the lagoon (a wonderful honeymoon keepsake). Browse the resort boutique for premium Maldivian souvenirs — lacquerwork, hand-woven items, and locally crafted jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: The grandest dinner of your trip — the resort's chef's table experience. Dine in the kitchen or a private dining room where the head chef personally prepares and presents a bespoke 7-course tasting menu inspired by your preferences and the finest seasonal ingredients. Paired with a curated wine and Champagne flight. A truly once-in-a-lifetime meal.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — a lavish spread at the main restaurant with made-to-order eggs, fresh seafood, tropical fruits, pastries, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside farewell lunch — tuna tartare, avocado and prawn salad, and a glass of chilled Sancerre
meals.dinner: Chef's table 7-course tasting menu — amuse-bouche, oysters, lobster consommé, Wagyu beef, mango sorbet, artisan cheese, and a passion fruit soufflé with Champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: The chef's table must be booked well in advance — ideally at the beginning of your stay. The underwater photographer session should also be pre-arranged. Ask for a printed photo album or USB drive of your images as a parting gift from the resort. Begin packing this evening.

day_by_day.morning: A bittersweet final morning — wake up early to watch the sunrise one last time from your villa deck. Enjoy a quiet in-villa farewell breakfast with your favorite items from the week. Take a final swim in your plunge pool or the lagoon. Your butler assists with luggage and checkout formalities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, enjoy a final coffee at the resort's lounge bar and exchange heartfelt farewells with the resort team. Board your private luxury speedboat or seaplane transfer back to Malé Velana International Airport. Arrive in time for your departure, carrying with you memories of an extraordinary 13-day Maldivian honeymoon.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — board your flight home, refreshed, deeply relaxed, and forever bonded by the magic of the Maldives.

meals.breakfast: Final in-villa breakfast — your favorites from the week, freshly prepared by the kitchen one last time
meals.lunch: Light airport lounge lunch or early lunch at the resort before transfer — keep it simple and easy for travel
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at your layover destination

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 12:00 noon — confirm with the resort if a late checkout is possible depending on your flight. Request a farewell amenity bag from the resort (many luxury properties provide guests with local treats, essential oils, and a handwritten note). Ensure all resort charges are reviewed and settled the evening before departure to avoid morning stress.
